Environment: Python 3.12.6, linux (pytest 8.4.2). Project: EnterpriseBench-t2dl4.

Source evidence: Two parse boundaries in scripts/cost_tracker.py:201 and lib/eb_metrics/retrieval_extraction.py:380 caught only json.JSONDecodeError. Verified by test execution (4 RED before fix, 177 GREEN after fix) on 2026-07-17. Bug filed as EnterpriseBench-t2dl4 (P1, pre-existing, found in Phase 4 of EnterpriseBench-4p5k security review).

Observed failure and caller recovery/error contract: json.loads raises THREE distinct exceptions at parse boundaries, not one. (1) json.JSONDecodeError — standard malformed JSON. (2) Bare ValueError — triggered in Python 3.11+ when an integer literal exceeds sys.int_info.default_max_str_digits (4300 digits); this is the CVE-2020-10735 mitigation. JSONDecodeError is a SUBCLASS of ValueError, so catching only JSONDecodeError does NOT catch bare ValueError. (3) RecursionError — triggered by deeply-nested structures (e.g. [[[[...]]]] at sufficient depth). Both (2) and (3) were confirmed to crash the caller in these two specific files rather than skipping the line, aborting cost reporting for the entire batch when any one trace line was malformed. The documented contract at this boundary ('a trace is third-party input') is to skip unreadable lines. Fix: catch (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError) and treat the line as malformed.

Limits and conditional transfer: The ValueError/int-string guard applies to Python 3.11+ only. The RecursionError path is version-independent but depth-sensitive. These two call sites were the only verified locations in this codebase; do not assume every json.loads boundary in other projects has the same recovery contract. Not a security issue in this project (internal harness reading its own traces). P1 robustness/availability bug.
